item.title: Danish Parliament passes food check as response to high prices
item.description: The Danish Parliament has passed a law for a tax-free “food check” to support over two million citizens following rising food prices. Approximately 4.5 billion DKK is allocated for the initiative. item.title: Sweden forces Russian drone away from carrier at Malmö
item.description: A Russian drone approached the French aircraft carrier “Charles de Gaulle” while it was docked in Malmö, Sweden. According to SVT, the Swedish military detected the drone and used jamming to disrupt its signals, causing it to fly away. The drone reportedly launched from a nearby Russian vessel. item.title: PM proposes wealth tax for the rich
item.description: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen has proposed a wealth tax for Denmark’s richest citizens. item.title: Danske Bank cuts 230 jobs in Denmark
item.description: Danske Bank has cut 420 positions across the bank, with 230 employees laid off in Denmark and 114 in Lithuania. The reductions, which also occurred to a lesser extent in other European countries, result from increased automation and simplification aimed at making the bank more digital and efficient. item.title: The international who is challenging the hierarchy of Dansk Bank from inside – “I’ve seen people working late into the night, driven by organizational pressure or a sense of pride”
item.description: Despite strong financial results, an employee from Bulgaria is calling for a shift in focus that addresses colleagues’ imposter syndrome, their fear of speaking up, and the so-called “golden cage” phenomenon.

item.title: More than expected seek compensation in Greenland spiral case after 1992
item.description: 209 women have applied for compensation from the Greenlandic government for receiving contraception without knowledge or consent after January 1, 1992, when Greenland assumed control of its healthcare from Denmark. Currently, 111 applications are being processed. This volume significantly exceeds initial expectations, causing delays to the assessment process originally scheduled for completion by February 2026. item.description: The digital mailbox e-Boks is launching “e-Boks ID,” a new login solution designed to compete with MitID and international providers like Facebook and Google.
